title: Rationale for Selection Criteria and Less Generous Compensation under VERS
what_it_is: Rationale for Selection Criteria and Less Generous Compensation under VERS

sections.label: VERS compensation questions to Minister
sections.summary: Questions ask how VERS compensation is defined, what protects homeowners with outstanding mortgages, and the rationale for less generous terms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) how does the Ministry define and quantify the less generous compensation terms of VERS as compared to SERS particularly in relation to a flat’s market value; (b) what safeguards will protect homeowners whose VERS compensation could be lower than their outstanding mortgage; and (c) what is the projected median cash top-up required for displaced households to secure replacement housing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development (a) what is the primary policy rationale for compensation under VERS being less generous than SERS; (b) how does the shift away from the SERS lottery effect support the goal of long-term housing affordability; and (c) what assurance can the Ministry provide that VERS will primarily serve as an orderly renewal programme and not a wealth-generating one.

sections.label: Second round of HIP upgrades
sections.summary: Older flats already had MUP or HIP upgrades, and a second round, HIP II, is planned for flats passing the 60-year mark.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: These older flats would have already benefited from one round of upgrades under the previous Main Upgrading Programme (MUP) or the current Home Improvement Programme (HIP) for flats that have passed the 30-year mark.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We plan to introduce a second round of upgrades via HIP II for flats which pass the 60-year mark.

sections.label: VERS sites selection timing
sections.summary: After the VERS framework and parameters are established, a few selected sites can start, likely in the first half of the next decade.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: After we have established the VERS framework and parameters, we can then start with a few selected sites, likely in the first half of the next decade.

sections.label: VERS compensation lower than SERS
sections.summary: Flats offered VERS have shorter remaining leases than those previously offered SERS, so overall VERS compensation would be lower.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Flats offered VERS will have shorter remaining leases compared to the flats which were previously offered SERS, so the overall compensation for VERS would be lower compared to SERS.

sections.label: VERS compensation varies across sites
sections.summary: Compensation would vary across VERS sites and flats, and MND and HDB will engage Singaporeans on draft proposals before finalising details.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: Just as how the valuation of flats varies today, the compensation amount would similarly vary across different VERS sites and flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We are also studying details such as the voting process and how to support the various demographic groups across different VERS sites with relocation options.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: MND and HDB will engage Singaporeans on the framework and policy parameters when we are ready with the draft proposals to take in further views and feedback before we finalise the policy and implementation details.

sections.label: Assurance for seniors' mortgages
sections.summary: The question asks how the public can be assured seniors will not be left with outstanding mortgages or forced to deplete retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: They would have been expecting to live in these flats until they pass on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Low Wu Yang Andre (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: So, how can we assure the public that we will consider these considerations when we try and ensure that these seniors are not left with, let us say, outstanding mortgages that the compensation amount cannot cover, or they are forced to deplete their retirement savings in order to top up with cash outlay, in order to secure replacement accommodation?

sections.label: Gatekeeping home purchases, VERS timing
sections.summary: Maintaining gatekeeping for home purchases means older flats reach VERS at 70 years or more, with residents mostly seniors who have paid off mortgages.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: If we can maintain the gatekeeping for people to buy homes that can last them for life, so by the time the flats reach the time that they need to go through VERS, which will be at least about 70 years or more, we would expect that most of the residents staying in these older flats would be seniors and hopefully, they would have already paid off their mortgages.

sections.label: NRP, HIP II and VERS voting
sections.summary: The more attractive HIP II and NRP are, the less likely residents may vote for VERS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Foo Cexiang (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: So, NRP, HIP II – these are important programmes.
However, the more attractive these programmes are, HIP II and NRP, the less likely you may have residents who will vote for VERS.

sections.label: HIP II upgrading older flats
sections.summary: HIP II at the 60-year mark invests in upgrading interiors of older flats to keep them safe and liveable, regardless of the VERS package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: This is something which we will have to pay careful attention to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We will share more details of HIP II when we are ready.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But the concept of HIP II is, say, at the 60-year and above mark, to be able to invest in upgrading the interiors of the older flats to keep them safe and liveable and to also pay attention to looking after the needs of the residents as they age together with the flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: That is something which, I think, we are quite clear.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: That regardless of what the package for VERS is, this objective of upgrading our older flats to keep them liveable, safe, upgrade our estates to keep our estates vibrant and liveable; that is something that we will do.
